title: finding(plugin-chatbot): the aiInitialMessages builder casts an authored `role: 'tool'` to the SDK's three roles, so in API mode a 'tool' role reaches the useChat store unfolded
body:
Found while measuring objectui#8426. Same `useMemo`, different suppression — objectui#8426 is about the `parts` array, this is about `role`. Out of that card's scope. ⛔ Not claimed.

## What

`packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useObjectChat.ts`, measured on `origin/main` @ `ca3942729`. Two casts inside the `aiInitialMessages` `useMemo` (`:545`):

- `:551` — `role: (msg.role || 'user') as 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'`
- `:576` — `role: normalized.role as 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'`

`msg.role` is the authoring `ChatMessage['role']`, which is `'user' | 'assistant' | 'system' | 'tool'` (`packages/types/src/complex.ts`). `normalizeMessages` (`useObjectChat.ts:422`) deliberately does not narrow it — its own doc comment says so at `:417-420`: "Roles are deliberately NOT narrowed here: an authored `'tool'` message keeps its authored role for the whole of the hook's surface and is folded to `'assistant'` only at the render seam."

So at runtime the object these two lines build carries `role: 'tool'` while declaring one of three roles it is not. In API mode that value is what seeds the AI SDK store (`:712`).

## Why it matters

The package already owns one expression of this fold, by name and by decision: `chatMessageAdapter.toRuntimeRole` (`packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chatMessageAdapter.ts:186`), whose doc records it as "the named decision (objectui#4399): an authored `'tool'` message renders as an assistant bubble". The render seam applies it. This builder does not — it asserts the narrowing instead of performing it, which is the same defect class objectui#4424 and objectui#8342 each removed one instance of.

Reachability: `renderer.tsx` passes `schema.messages` straight through as `initialMessages` (`:79`, `:268`, `:406`), and the authoring `ChatMessage` accepts `role: 'tool'` — `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/useObjectChat.honestMessages.test.tsx:157-167` authors exactly such a message today. That test runs in LOCAL mode, where the builder's output is never handed to `useChat`; the API-mode leg (`api` set plus an authored `'tool'` message) is the unexercised one.

Not measured here: what the AI SDK store or the backend does with an out-of-union role. The finding is that the value is out of union and the compiler was told not to look.

## Fix shape (not ruled)

Replace both casts with `toRuntimeRole(...)`, which already returns exactly the three roles, and delete the assertions. That is a behaviour change on the API-mode leg (an authored `'tool'` message would seed the store as `'assistant'` rather than `'tool'`), which is why this is filed rather than folded into objectui#8426.

## Dedup

`search_issues` over this repo for the builder's casts and the authored role — 5 hits, all read, all closed: objectui#8342, objectui#8378, objectui#8214, objectui#4424, objectui#4437. None names these two `role` casts.

## Related

objectui#8426 · objectui#8378 · objectui#4424 · objectui#4399
